verbatim: Desde Google Cloud nos complace anunciar la apertura de nuestra región de nube número 41 en Querétaro, México, la cual ya está en operación.

Se espera que como resultado de esta nueva región, el aumento en la adopción de la nube y la productividad que brinda generen más de 100,000 empleos y contribuyan con más de $11,000 millones de dólares al PIB de México para 2030.

Otro ejemplo es el programa "Súbete a la nube" que creamos en México en asociación con el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) con un enfoque en las mujeres y la región sur del país. Hasta la fecha, 12,500 personas se han registrado para recibir capacitación en habilidades digitales esenciales en computación en la nube.
Seattle--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Amazon Web Services (AWS), an Amazon.com, Inc. company (NASDAQ: AMZN), today announced the launch of the AWS Mexico (Central) Region.
As part of its long-term commitment, AWS is planning to invest more than $5 billion in Mexico over 15 years.

AWS estimates the construction and ongoing operation of the new AWS Region will add approximately $10 billion to Mexico’s gross domestic product (GDP) and support an average of more than 7,000 full-time equivalent jobs at external businesses annually.
AWS has also launched a $300,000 AWS InCommunities Fund in Queretaro to help local groups, schools, and organizations initiate new community projects.

Querétaro: In partnership with Aquestia, we installed valves, controllers, and communication equipment in 11 measured districts, benefiting 12,500 people and projecting savings of 130 million liters per year.

AWS, in collaboration with the State Government and the Municipal Government of Querétaro, launched the Amazon Think Big Space in 2026, with the purpose of providing students, educators, and community members a space to explore ideas through interactive technical education and cloud computing training.
